key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match the function class of wider multi-qubit circuits with the same encoding budget, but first-order optimization is much harder because all parameters are phase-locked into too few tangent directions.
engineering_relevance: For quantum model design, trading qubit width for depth may preserve expressivity while significantly increasing training difficulty, especially under gradient-based optimizers.
method: Analyzed angle-encoded variational circuits as truncated Fourier series for 1D inputs.
Proved a tangent-space/phase-locking limitation for single-qubit serial circuits versus multi-qubit controls at equal encoding budget.
Compared optimization success on synthetic flat-spectrum targets and real-world time series under gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg–Marquardt.
evidence_signal: Across 100 runs, the serial circuit was far less likely to reach the optimum than the control, e.g., at E=32 it converged in 3/53/83 runs versus 99/100/100, and on real series it lagged similarly while sometimes showing up to ~1.5× worse test error under Adam.
watch_item: The advantage of wider circuits is shown under the paper’s specific encoding budgets, optimizer choices, and 1D angle-encoded setup, so the conclusion may not transfer unchanged to other ansätze or higher-dimensional inputs.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
